Brief: Tell me about the Rosetta mission and what it found at comet 67P. — about Surface changes

1. During Rosetta's lifetime, many changes were observed on the comet's surface, particularly when the comet was close to perihelion.
2. These changes included evolving patterns of circular shapes in smooth terrains that at some point grew in size by a few meters per day.
3. A fracture in the neck region was also observed to grow in size; boulders tens of meters wide were displaced, sometimes travelling more than 100 meters; and patches of the ground were removed to expose new features.
4. A number of collapsing cliffs have also been observed.
5. One notable example in December 2015 was captured by Rosetta's NAVCAM as a bright patch of light shining from the comet.
6. Rosetta scientists determined that a large cliff had collapsed, making it the first landslide on a comet known to be associated with an outburst of activity.
7. An apparent outburst of the comet was observed on 14 November 2021.
8. According to the researchers, "At the time of the outburst discovery with ZTF, the comet was 1.23 au from the Sun and 0.42 au from the Earth.
9. The comet's last perihelion passage was on 2021 Nov 2.".
